blocks.en: "I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith." — 2 Timothy 4:7 (NKJV)

blocks.en: Introduction — The Last Thing Is the Main Thing
blocks.es_reference: Introducción — Lo último es lo principal

blocks.en: We have come a long way together. We have talked about vision and structure, about money and people, about buildings and laws, about planting and succession. And now, at the end, we arrive at the one subject that holds all the others together and without which every one of them collapses: the heart of the leader himself. For a man may master every skill in this course and still make shipwreck of his ministry, because the deadliest dangers a leader faces are not out in the budget or the building. They are inside his own chest. So we close where we should have begun, with the man in the mirror. The first unit said leadership is character before technique. This last unit says the same thing again, only now we have walked far enough to feel its weight. Guard your heart, brother. Everything else you have learned is built on it.
blocks.es_reference: Hemos recorrido un largo camino juntos. Hemos hablado de visión y estructura, de dinero y personas, de edificios y leyes, de plantación y sucesión. Y ahora, al final, llegamos al único tema que sostiene a todos los demás y sin el cual cada uno de ellos se derrumba: el corazón del líder mismo. Porque un hombre puede dominar toda destreza de este curso y aun así naufragar en su ministerio, pues los peligros más mortales que un líder enfrenta no están allá afuera en el presupuesto o el edificio. Están dentro de su propio pecho. Así que cerramos donde debimos haber comenzado, con el hombre en el espejo. La primera unidad dijo que el liderazgo es carácter antes que técnica. Esta última unidad dice lo mismo otra vez, solo que ahora hemos caminado lo suficiente para sentir su peso. Guarde su corazón, hermano. Todo lo demás que ha aprendido se edifica sobre él.

blocks.en: "Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it spring the issues of life." — Proverbs 4:23 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Sobre toda cosa guardada, guarda tu corazón; porque de él mana la vida." — Proverbios 4:23 (RVG)

blocks.en: I. Integrity: One Life, Not Two
blocks.es_reference: I. Integridad: una sola vida, no dos

blocks.en: The first guardian of a long ministry is integrity, and the word itself tells you what it means. Integrity is integration — being one whole person, the same man in the pulpit and in the kitchen, the same man when the crowd is watching and when no one is. The opposite of integrity is not merely dishonesty; it is a divided life, a man who has learned to be two people, the public saint and the private stranger. That division will widen in silence for years, and then one day it will tear open and destroy everything.
blocks.es_reference: El primer guardián de un ministerio duradero es la integridad, y la palabra misma le dice lo que significa. Integridad es integración — ser una sola persona entera, el mismo hombre en el púlpito y en la cocina, el mismo hombre cuando la multitud observa y cuando nadie lo hace. Lo opuesto de la integridad no es meramente la deshonestidad; es una vida dividida, un hombre que ha aprendido a ser dos personas, el santo público y el extraño privado. Esa división se ensanchará en silencio por años, y luego un día se rasgará y destruirá todo.

blocks.en: Scripture's word for the leader is "blameless" (1 Timothy 3:2) — not sinless, for no man is, but with no glaring gap between what he proclaims and how he lives, nothing hidden that would shame him if it came to light. David, for all his terrible failures, is finally remembered this way: he shepherded the people "according to the integrity of his heart, and guided them by the skillfulness of his hands" (Psalm 78:72). Mark the order in that verse — the integrity of the heart comes before the skill of the hands. This whole course has been about the skill of the hands, and the skill matters. But it sits on the heart, and a skillful hand attached to a divided heart will, in the end, only do more damage. Be one man. Live one life. What you are in secret is what you really are.
blocks.es_reference: La palabra de la Escritura para el líder es "irreprensible" (1 Timoteo 3:2) — no sin pecado, pues ningún hombre lo es, sino sin una brecha evidente entre lo que proclama y cómo vive, nada oculto que lo avergonzaría si saliera a la luz. David, con todos sus terribles fracasos, es recordado al final así: apacentó al pueblo "conforme a la integridad de su corazón; los pastoreó con la pericia de sus manos" (Salmo 78:72). Note el orden en ese versículo — la integridad del corazón viene antes que la destreza de las manos. Todo este curso ha tratado de la destreza de las manos, y la destreza importa. Pero descansa sobre el corazón, y una mano diestra unida a un corazón dividido, al final, solo hará más daño. Sea un solo hombre. Viva una sola vida. Lo que usted es en secreto es lo que realmente es.

blocks.en: Be one man. Live one life. What you are in secret is what you really are.
blocks.es_reference: Sea un solo hombre. Viva una sola vida. Lo que usted es en secreto es lo que realmente es.

blocks.en: II. The Watch Over the Heart
blocks.es_reference: II. La guardia sobre el corazón

blocks.en: Where does a leader fall? Almost always in one of three places, and the wise man names them so he can watch them. The old summary is blunt and accurate: gold, glory, and girls — money, pride, and sex. We have already faced the love of money back in Unit 5; here we simply add that it has never stopped claiming leaders and never will. The second is glory — the slow swelling of pride, the love of the applause, the subtle shift from serving God to feeding the self that serves God so visibly. "Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall" (Proverbs 16:18). And the third is sexual sin, which has laid low more gifted ministries than perhaps any other, and against which the only reliable strategy is the one Joseph used: he "fled" (Genesis 39:12). Not negotiated, not lingered, not tested his own strength — fled.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Dónde cae un líder? Casi siempre en uno de tres lugares, y el sabio los nombra para poder vigilarlos. El viejo resumen es franco y certero: oro, gloria y mujeres — dinero, orgullo y sexo. Ya enfrentamos el amor al dinero allá en la Unidad 5; aquí solo añadimos que nunca ha dejado de reclamar líderes y nunca lo hará. El segundo es la gloria — el lento hinchamiento del orgullo, el amor al aplauso, el sutil giro de servir a Dios a alimentar al yo que sirve a Dios tan visiblemente. "Antes del quebrantamiento es la soberbia; y antes de la caída la altivez de espíritu" (Proverbios 16:18). Y el tercero es el pecado sexual, que ha derribado más ministerios dotados que quizá ningún otro, y contra el cual la única estrategia confiable es la que usó José: "huyó" (Génesis 39:12). No negoció, no se demoró, no probó su propia fuerza — huyó.

blocks.en: So mount a deliberate watch at exactly these gates. The leader who thinks he is the exception, who believes his gifting or his calling makes him immune, is the man already halfway to the fall, for "let him who thinks he stands take heed lest he fall" (1 Corinthians 10:12). Build real guards into your life while you are still strong: accountability to men who can ask you hard questions and will, honesty about your own weak places, and a holy fear that never quite believes you are beyond falling. The watch you keep over your own heart is the most important administration you will ever do.
blocks.es_reference: Así que monte una guardia deliberada exactamente en estas puertas. El líder que se cree la excepción, que cree que su don o su llamado lo hace inmune, es el hombre que ya está a medio camino de la caída, porque "el que piensa estar firme, mire que no caiga" (1 Corintios 10:12). Edifique guardas reales en su vida mientras todavía es fuerte: rendir cuentas a hombres que puedan hacerle preguntas difíciles y las harán, honestidad sobre sus propios puntos débiles, y un santo temor que nunca llegue del todo a creer que está más allá de caer. La guardia que usted mantiene sobre su propio corazón es la administración más importante que jamás hará.

blocks.en: "Let him who thinks he stands take heed lest he fall." — 1 Corinthians 10:12 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "El que piensa estar firme, mire que no caiga." — 1 Corintios 10:12 (RVG)

blocks.en: III. The Sabbath the Leader Skips
blocks.es_reference: III. El reposo que el líder se salta

blocks.en: Now to a sin that hides as a virtue, and I must press it because it may be the one you least suspect in yourself: the refusal to rest. God built rest into the very fabric of creation and then commanded it — "Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy" (Exodus 20:8) — not as a suggestion for the weak but as a rhythm for everyone, written into the Ten Commandments beside "you shall not murder" and "you shall not steal." Yet many a faithful leader breaks this command continually and even boasts of it, wearing his exhaustion like a badge of devotion.
blocks.es_reference: Ahora a un pecado que se esconde como virtud, y debo insistir porque puede ser el que menos sospeche en usted mismo: la negativa a descansar. Dios incorporó el reposo en la trama misma de la creación y luego lo mandó — "Acordarte has del día del reposo, para santificarlo" (Éxodo 20:8) — no como una sugerencia para los débiles sino como un ritmo para todos, escrito en los Diez Mandamientos junto a "no matarás" y "no hurtarás." Sin embargo, muchos líderes fieles quebrantan este mandato continuamente y hasta se jactan de ello, llevando su agotamiento como una insignia de devoción.

blocks.en: Hear the Lord, who knew His disciples were running past empty: "Come aside by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a while" (Mark 6:31). That is a command of Christ as surely as any other. The leader who will not rest is not more spiritual than the rest of us; he is, in fact, telling a quiet lie with his life — the lie that the work depends on him and not on God, that if he stops, the kingdom stops. It does not. Even the Lord of all the earth rested on the seventh day, not from weakness but to teach us. Refusing rest is not humility; it is a subtle pride that thinks itself indispensable, and it leads straight to the burnout that ends ministries early. Take the rest God commands. Keep a Sabbath. Sleep. Step away. The God who calls you to the work also commands you to lay it down regularly — and trusting Him enough to stop is its own act of faith.
blocks.es_reference: Oiga al Señor, que sabía que sus discípulos corrían más allá del vacío: "Venid vosotros aparte a un lugar desierto, y reposad un poco" (Marcos 6:31). Ese es un mandato de Cristo tan ciertamente como cualquier otro. El líder que no descansa no es más espiritual que el resto de nosotros; está, de hecho, diciendo una mentira callada con su vida — la mentira de que la obra depende de él y no de Dios, de que si se detiene, el reino se detiene. No es así. Aun el Señor de toda la tierra reposó en el séptimo día, no por debilidad sino para enseñarnos. Rehusar el descanso no es humildad; es un orgullo sutil que se cree indispensable, y conduce directo al agotamiento que termina los ministerios temprano. Tome el descanso que Dios manda. Guarde un día de reposo. Duerma. Apártese. El Dios que lo llama a la obra también le manda dejarla regularmente — y confiar en Él lo suficiente para detenerse es en sí mismo un acto de fe.

blocks.en: IV. The Inner Life Behind the Public Work
blocks.es_reference: IV. La vida interior detrás de la obra pública

blocks.en: Why do leaders fall, burn out, and lose their integrity? Almost always because the public life outgrew the private one. The ministry got bigger and bigger while the secret walk with God got thinner and thinner, until one day there was a great public ministry standing on almost no private foundation, and it could not bear its own weight. The leader had become a professional handler of holy things and quietly stopped being a worshiper.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Por qué caen los líderes, se agotan y pierden su integridad? Casi siempre porque la vida pública creció más que la privada. El ministerio se hizo cada vez más grande mientras el andar secreto con Dios se hizo cada vez más delgado, hasta que un día hubo un gran ministerio público de pie sobre casi ningún fundamento privado, y no pudo soportar su propio peso. El líder se había vuelto un manipulador profesional de cosas santas y calladamente dejó de ser un adorador.

blocks.en: Guard the inner life as the source of everything else. The Lord was explicit: "He who abides in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit; for without Me you can do nothing" (John 15:5). Nothing — not the preaching, not the leading, not the administration this whole course has taught. The branch that stops drawing sap from the vine keeps its leaves for a while and then quietly dies, often without anyone noticing until the fruit is gone. So tend the hidden things no congregation ever sees: your own prayer, your own reading of the Word as food and not just as sermon fuel, your own repentance, your own communion with God. The size of your public ministry should never outrun the depth of your private walk. Keep the secret life larger than the visible one, and the visible one will have something real to stand on.
blocks.es_reference: Guarde la vida interior como la fuente de todo lo demás. El Señor fue explícito: "El que permanece en mí, y yo en él, éste lleva mucho fruto; porque sin mí nada podéis hacer" (Juan 15:5). Nada — ni la predicación, ni el liderazgo, ni la administración que todo este curso ha enseñado. La rama que deja de extraer savia de la vid conserva sus hojas por un tiempo y luego muere calladamente, a menudo sin que nadie lo note hasta que el fruto se ha ido. Así que cuide las cosas ocultas que ninguna congregación ve jamás: su propia oración, su propia lectura de la Palabra como alimento y no solo como combustible para sermones, su propio arrepentimiento, su propia comunión con Dios. El tamaño de su ministerio público nunca debe sobrepasar la profundidad de su andar privado. Mantenga la vida secreta más grande que la visible, y la visible tendrá algo real sobre lo cual sostenerse.

blocks.en: The size of your public ministry should never outrun the depth of your private walk.
blocks.es_reference: El tamaño de su ministerio público nunca debe sobrepasar la profundidad de su andar privado.

blocks.en: V. Running to Finish
blocks.es_reference: V. Correr para terminar

blocks.en: Scripture compares the life of faith to a race, and it is not a sprint but a long, grueling distance run, where the danger is not a bad start but a slow quitting somewhere in the exhausting middle miles. "Let us run with endurance the race that is set before us" (Hebrews 12:1). Endurance — the long obedience, the refusal to drift away or burn out or grow cynical or simply coast to a stop. Many begin the ministry with fire. The honor goes to those who are still running, still faithful, still tender toward God, at the end.
blocks.es_reference: La Escritura compara la vida de fe con una carrera, y no es una de velocidad sino una larga y agotadora carrera de distancia, donde el peligro no es un mal comienzo sino un lento abandono en algún punto de las extenuantes millas del medio. "Corramos con paciencia la carrera que tenemos por delante" (Hebreos 12:1). Paciencia — la larga obediencia, la negativa a desviarse o agotarse o volverse cínico o sencillamente detenerse por inercia. Muchos comienzan el ministerio con fuego. La honra es para quienes siguen corriendo, siguen fieles, siguen tiernos hacia Dios, al final.

blocks.en: This is why we must say plainly that not everyone finishes well. Scripture itself records men who began with promise and ended in ruin — a Saul who started humble and ended consumed by jealousy and fear, a Solomon granted wisdom beyond any man who let foreign loves turn his heart in his old age. A good beginning guarantees nothing about the end. Demas was once Paul's fellow worker, and the saddest little phrase in all his letters is the epitaph: "Demas has forsaken me, having loved this present world" (2 Timothy 4:10). He did not fall to scandal. He simply loved the world more, a little at a time, until he drifted off and was gone. Finishing well is not automatic. It is the fruit of a thousand daily choices to keep the heart, keep the watch, keep the rest, keep the inner life, and keep running. Begin well, yes — but set your face, from the start, on ending well.
blocks.es_reference: Por esto debemos decir con claridad que no todos terminan bien. La Escritura misma registra hombres que comenzaron con promesa y terminaron en ruina — un Saúl que empezó humilde y terminó consumido por los celos y el temor, un Salomón a quien se dio sabiduría más que a ningún hombre y que dejó que amores extraños torcieran su corazón en su vejez. Un buen comienzo no garantiza nada sobre el final. Demas fue una vez colaborador de Pablo, y la frase más triste en todas sus cartas es el epitafio: "Demas me ha desamparado, amando este mundo presente" (2 Timoteo 4:10). No cayó por escándalo. Sencillamente amó al mundo más, poco a poco, hasta que se apartó y se fue. Terminar bien no es automático. Es el fruto de mil decisiones diarias de guardar el corazón, guardar la vigilancia, guardar el descanso, guardar la vida interior, y seguir corriendo. Comience bien, sí — pero ponga su rostro, desde el principio, en terminar bien.

blocks.en: "Demas has forsaken me, having loved this present world." — 2 Timothy 4:10 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Demas me ha desamparado, amando este mundo presente." — 2 Timoteo 4:10 (RVG)

blocks.en: VI. Well Done: The Only Approval That Lasts
blocks.es_reference: VI. Bien hecho: la única aprobación que dura

blocks.en: So fix your eyes on the finish, and on the only verdict that will finally matter. At the end of his life Paul sat in a Roman prison, abandoned by most, with nothing the world counts as success — no megachurch, no monument, no comfortable retirement. And he wrote some of the most triumphant words ever penned: "I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith. Finally, there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous Judge, will give to me on that Day" (2 Timothy 4:7–8).
blocks.es_reference: Así que fije sus ojos en la meta, y en el único veredicto que finalmente importará. Al final de su vida Pablo estaba sentado en una prisión romana, abandonado por la mayoría, sin nada que el mundo cuente como éxito — sin megaiglesia, sin monumento, sin un retiro cómodo. Y escribió algunas de las palabras más triunfantes jamás escritas: "He peleado la buena batalla, he acabado la carrera, he guardado la fe. Por lo demás, me está guardada la corona de justicia, la cual me dará el Señor, juez justo, en aquel día" (2 Timoteo 4:7–8).

blocks.en: There is the goal of everything this course has tried to build in you. Not a crowd's applause, which fades before the parking lot empties. Not numbers, which the next generation forgets. Not your name on a building. But to stand at last before the Chief Shepherd we met back in Unit 2, the One who owns the flock and purchased it with His blood, and to hear from His lips the only words that will matter on that Day: "Well done, good and faithful servant... enter into the joy of your lord" (Matthew 25:21). Notice He does not say "well done, good and successful servant," or "gifted," or "famous." Faithful. That is the whole of it. So lead the church with all the skill this course could give you — cast the vision, build the structure, steward the money, shepherd the people, guard the house, plant and multiply and prepare the one who follows you. But above all of it and underneath all of it, keep your heart, walk with your God, rest in His sufficiency, and run all the way to the line. Be faithful to the end, brother. And one day, from the only mouth whose approval can never be taken away, you will hear, "Well done." That is finishing well. There is nothing better to live for, and nothing else worth giving your life to.
blocks.es_reference: Ahí está la meta de todo lo que este curso ha tratado de edificar en usted. No el aplauso de una multitud, que se desvanece antes de que el estacionamiento se vacíe. No los números, que la siguiente generación olvida. No su nombre sobre un edificio. Sino estar al fin delante del Príncipe de los pastores que conocimos allá en la Unidad 2, Aquel que posee el rebaño y lo compró con su sangre, y oír de sus labios las únicas palabras que importarán en aquel día: "Bien, buen siervo y fiel... entra en el gozo de tu señor" (Mateo 25:21). Note que no dice "bien, buen siervo y exitoso," ni "dotado," ni "famoso." Fiel. Eso es todo. Así que dirija la iglesia con toda la destreza que este curso pudo darle — eche la visión, edifique la estructura, administre el dinero, pastoree al pueblo, guarde la casa, plante y multiplique y prepare al que le sigue. Pero por encima de todo ello y por debajo de todo ello, guarde su corazón, ande con su Dios, descanse en su suficiencia, y corra hasta la línea. Sea fiel hasta el fin, hermano. Y un día, de la única boca cuya aprobación nunca puede serle quitada, oirá: "Bien hecho." Eso es terminar bien. No hay nada mejor por qué vivir, y nada más que valga la pena darle su vida.

blocks.en: He does not say "successful," or "gifted," or "famous." Faithful. That is the whole of it.
blocks.es_reference: No dice "exitoso," ni "dotado," ni "famoso." Fiel. Eso es todo.

Jesus told His weary disciples, "Come aside by yourselves to a deserted place and ____ a while" (Mark 6:31).
"He who abides in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit; for without Me you can do ____" (John 15:5).
Paul's former fellow worker ____ did not fall to scandal but drifted away, "having loved this present world" (2 Timothy 4:10).
The only approval that lasts is the Lord's "Well done, good and ____ servant" (Matthew 25:21), not "successful" or "gifted."

sa.prompt: Explain what 'integrity' means in this unit and why the heart matters more than skill.
sa.model: Integrity means integration — being one whole person, the same man in public and in secret, not a divided life with a public saint and a private stranger. The unit grounds it in Psalm 78:72, where David led by the integrity of his heart before the skill of his hands. The heart matters more than skill because a skillful hand attached to a divided heart only does more damage in the end; what a leader is in secret is what he really is, so one life lived whole is the foundation the skill stands on.

sa.prompt: Name the three classic places a leader falls and describe the watch he must keep.
sa.model: Leaders most often fall in three places summarized as gold, glory, and girls — money, pride, and sexual sin. Against money the leader stays a faithful steward; against the glory of swelling pride he remembers that pride goes before a fall; against sexual sin he flees as Joseph fled. The watch means mounting deliberate guards at these gates: accountability to men who will ask hard questions, honesty about weak places, and a holy fear that never believes he is beyond falling, since the one who thinks he stands must take heed lest he fall.

sa.prompt: Why does this unit treat the refusal to rest as a sin rather than a virtue?
sa.model: The refusal to rest hides as a virtue but is really disobedience, because rest is commanded: 'Remember the Sabbath day,' written into the Ten Commandments, and Christ Himself said come aside and rest a while. The leader who will not rest tells a quiet lie with his life — that the work depends on him and not on God, that if he stops the kingdom stops. That is not humility but a subtle pride that thinks itself indispensable, and it leads straight to the burnout that ends ministries early, so taking the rest God commands is itself an act of faith.

sa.prompt: Using John 15:5, explain why the inner life must stay larger than the public ministry.
sa.model: Jesus said the one who abides in Him bears much fruit, for without Him you can do nothing — not the preaching, leading, or administration. Leaders fall when the public life outgrows the private one, so that a great ministry stands on almost no private foundation and cannot bear its own weight. The branch cut from the vine keeps its leaves a while and then dies. So the leader must guard the hidden inner life no one sees — his own prayer, his reading of the Word as food, his repentance and communion — keeping the secret life larger than the visible so the public work has something real to stand on.

sa.prompt: What does it mean that the Christian life is a race run with endurance, and what is the real danger?
sa.model: Hebrews 12:1 calls the life of faith a race run with endurance, and it is not a sprint but a long, grueling distance run. The real danger is not a bad start but a slow quitting in the exhausting middle miles — drifting away, burning out, growing cynical, or coasting to a stop. Many begin with fire, but the honor goes to those still running and still tender toward God at the end. Finishing well is the fruit of a thousand daily choices to keep the heart and keep running, so the leader must set his face on enduring all the way to the line.

sa.prompt: What does the example of Demas teach about how a leader can fail to finish well?
sa.model: Demas was once Paul's fellow worker, but the epitaph is that he forsook Paul, having loved this present world. The lesson is that he did not fall to a sudden scandal; he simply loved the world more, a little at a time, drifting gradually until he was gone. This warns that finishing well is not automatic and a leader can be lost not by one dramatic sin but by a slow drift of the affections, so the leader must guard against the gradual love of the world that quietly pulls a man off the race before the end.

sa.prompt: Contrast the world's measures of success with the verdict the leader should live for.
sa.model: The world measures success by a crowd's applause that fades before the parking lot empties, by numbers the next generation forgets, and by a name on a building. But the only verdict the leader should live for is the Master's word, 'Well done, good and faithful servant.' He does not say successful, gifted, or famous, but faithful — faithfulness is the whole of it. So the leader leads with all his skill yet fixes his eyes not on applause or numbers but on hearing 'well done' from the Chief Shepherd, the only approval that can never be taken away.

sa.prompt: How does this capstone unit tie the leader's heart back to the rest of the course?
sa.model: The capstone says the last thing is the main thing: a man may master every skill in the course and still wreck his ministry, because all the technique sits on the character of the heart. It deliberately returns to Unit 1, which taught character before technique, and now says the same thing with the weight of the whole course behind it. The vision, structure, money, people, buildings, and succession are all the skill of the hands, but they are built on the heart; guard the heart and the rest has a foundation, lose it and everything else collapses.

sa.prompt: Why must a leader guard against thinking he is the exception who cannot fall?
sa.model: The leader who believes his gifting or calling makes him immune is already halfway to the fall, for the one who thinks he stands must take heed lest he fall. Presuming to be the exception drops the watch over the heart at exactly the moment it is most needed, since the sense of immunity is itself the danger. So the leader stays humble and builds real guards while he is still strong — accountability, honesty about weak places, and a holy fear that never quite believes he is beyond falling — treating his own heart as something that must be watched, not trusted.

sa.prompt: Summarize the unit's final charge: what should a leader do above and beneath all his skill?
sa.model: The final charge is to lead the church with all the skill the course gave — vision, structure, money, people, the house, planting and succession — but above and beneath all of it to keep the heart, walk with God, rest in His sufficiency, and run all the way to the line. The leader must be faithful to the end, because the skill of the hands stands on the integrity of the heart. The aim of everything is to keep running, keep the watch, keep the rest and the inner life, and finish well so as to hear 'well done' from the only mouth whose approval lasts.
